prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1362; do not mention it.)
text:
I am writing to advise that this office now represents the injured party in connection with the collision described in your file. The incident involved a low-speed head-on impact, and our client sustained injuries that are being evaluated and treated. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or in person.

We request that you provide the bodily injury liability limits under the policy covering your insured, along with any declarations page or other documentation confirming the coverage in force on the date of loss. Please also confirm whether any additional coverage, such as umbrella or excess coverage, may apply.

We further ask that your company preserve all evidence relating to this loss. This includes photographs, vehicle damage appraisals, event data recorder information, recorded statements, claim notes, repair records, and any communications with the other parties involved. Please treat this letter as formal notice of the need to retain these materials until this matter is fully resolved.
